interpretations.rationale: Current account. Source-settled mechanism: the actor publishes every observed transition with `event_tx.send(..).await` inside `detect_and_emit_events` (actor.rs:169-199), awaited from the tick arm of the single `run` select loop (actor.rs:665-711), on the channel spawn_actor builds as `async_channel::bounded(RuntimeConfig::event_capacity)` (handle.rs:295-323; knob handle.rs:34-35, default 1024 handle.rs:74). The handle owns a receiver from construction, so an application that never consumes the event stream still leaves it unread, and `subscribe_events` only hands out clones of that same channel (handle.rs:254-259). A send that cannot fit parks the actor task, which then cannot run op.tick() (election heartbeats, resends, batch flushes), cannot handle incoming messages, and cannot answer any Command - including the append_notify Timeout that drain_notifiers would have produced on that same tick path (actor.rs:201-222; endpoint documented at handle.rs:114-137). The crate's sibling egress paths avoid this with try_send (drain_outgoing_buf; push_to_sub/push_to_all_subs), and its own regression test states the invariant for the outgoing channel. Retained support - execution ff4511e8f6684444b8b1ec403335f9f8 (experiment 1a5428f0aa284eb1a2a3f1a083fcb052-experiment, exit 0, both selected tests passed, no parsing errors), parsed events 2,3,4 for the unconsumed case and 0,1 for the control: event 2 `unconsumed_event_bound_reached` {nodes_full:3, nodes:3, event_capacity:64} shows all three nodes reached the bound with live receivers; event 3 `actor_parked` {node:1, samples_without_reply:10, reply_budget_ms:200, permanently_parked:true} shows a node whose actor never answered a `decided_idx` command across ten 200ms samples; event 4 `append_notify_endpoint_withheld` {node:1, per_call_deadline_ms:300, actor_timeout_ms:1500, outer_wait_ms:4000, resolved:false} shows that node never even reached the documented failure endpoint; in the same run, events 0 and 1 `control_actors_responsive` {nodes_answering:3, nodes:3} and `control_append_notify` {origin:2, succeeded:true, idx:2} show the identical cluster with the only difference that the event streams are drained keeps every node answering and decides a follower's proposal. The comparison therefore holds: with an unconsumed bounded event channel the actor loop is parked and its command endpoints are withheld, and with the same configuration and a consumed stream it is not. Scope of the defect asserted: a node whose client does not consume its event stream stops participating (no ticks, no message handling, no command replies) once it has observed event_capacity transitions, for any finite capacity; the probe reaches that bound at 64 to stay inside a bounded window, and the mechanism is capacity-independent because the send awaits whenever the channel holds capacity events. Counter-limitations kept in force: (a) the trigger is client-side usage and no snapshot source states a drain obligation, so the finding rests on the handle-method contract (every Command reply, and the documented Timeout) plus the deliberate non-blocking design of the sibling egress paths; (b) a dropped receiver unblocks the actor (the send error is ignored), so the stall lasts exactly as long as a live receiver exists; (c) the evidence is node-local - the bound was reached at 64, the parked set is 'at least one node' (the probe asserts all three channels full but only one permanently parked), and no quorum-level consequence (leadership churn caused by the silent node, or the cluster losing this participant) is measured.
limitations: Capacity-independence and practical reachability at the default 1024 are argued from source, not observed: the execution reached the bound at event_capacity=64.
Only node-local endpoints are witnessed (command round-trips, and the withheld append_notify endpoint); the cluster-level consequence of losing this participant is not measured.
The parked set is reported as all channels full plus at least one permanently parked node; the probe does not establish how many nodes park in a given schedule.

scope.description: Bounded, deterministic probe of whether a lost follower Accepted reply is repaired by the protocol's own resend/retry machinery within a window of 100 resend periods, or only by an unrelated later proposal.
assumptions: 2-node cluster so the write quorum is the leader's own acceptance plus exactly one follower receipt: one dropped message is enough to hide the quorum from the leader
error-free memory storage, FIFO delivery of everything else, no reordering, no crash and no leadership change during the window
one logical step per node equals one tick(), so the 500-step window contains 100 of the configured 5-tick resend periods for both roles

experiment.prefix: Deterministic in-process simulation of the core crate: two real OmniPaxos instances (pid 1,2; configuration_id 1; MemoryStorage; error-free storage) built by OmniPaxosConfig::build, never run concurrently - the harness drives them manually: each step calls tick() on both, drains take_outgoing_messages() into a FIFO, and delivers every message to the receiver's handle_incoming, except that it deliberately discards exactly one PaxosMsg::Accepted (the follower's receipt). Node 1 has leader_priority 1 so the election is deterministic; election_tick_timeout 3, resend_message_tick_timeout 5, batch_size 1. Case lost_accepted_leaves_entry_undecided: elect (both nodes Leader/Follower in the accept phase), append one entry at the leader, drop the follower's Accepted, then run 100 resend periods of ticks (500 steps) with everything else delivered; it emits CA_EVENT lost_accepted_window {steps,resend_periods,produced,dropped,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx,follower_accepted_idx,follower_holds_undecided_entry,leader_still_stable} and asserts exactly one Accepted was dropped, the follower really holds the entry as Undecided at index 0 with accepted_idx 1, the leader and the follower are both still at decided index 0, and the leader is still the stable leader. It then appends a second entry on the same state and emits CA_EVENT later_proposal_repairs {steps_until_decided,leader_decided_idx,follower_decided_idx}. Case delivered_accepted_decides is the control: identical, the receipt is delivered, and the entry must be decided inside the same bounded window (CA_EVENT delivered_accepted_decides). The prerequisite the probe relies on is not 'some message was dropped' but the actual per-message operands: which message kinds were produced and which was discarded are printed in the event.
